title: SwiftData: @Model CRUD
hints: Mark the class `@Model`; create a `ModelContainer` with `isStoredInMemoryOnly: true`.
Insert with `context.insert`, delete with `context.delete`, mutate properties directly.
jsBridge: SwiftData's `@Model` turns a class into a persisted entity, and `ModelContext` inserts, fetches and saves. It's Prisma/TypeORM-level ergonomics on top of Core Data, with Swift macros instead of a schema file.

compass.q: Prisma schema file + generated client vs SwiftData `@Model` macro: where does the schema live in each?
Why must `@Model` types be classes, not structs?
SwiftData autosave vs calling `try context.save()`: when does unsaved data get lost?
`@Query` in a view vs fetching in a view model: which does Apple's sample code prefer, and why do architecture purists object?
